title: What is your workflow for designing the game UIUX?
author: Chocoweb88
selftext:
Hi everyone. I started learning game development with Claude and is currently using Unity to build my mobile card game. The gameplay logic is fine, the animation is a future target for me. But the uiux, the button placement , the art style following a brand guideline, i just can't seem to get Claude to work it smoothly. Minor hiccups and misplacements and recalibration non stop. And im starting to wonder if I am doing this right.

What is your recommended workflow for uiux design? My current workflow is using Claude and Claude design to finalize the brand guideline (colors, fonts, themes etc) use image generation tools to generate the assets (Claude provide the prompts, I eyeball and pick the one match my vision) and then use Code to build Unity tools that build the in game layout and import the assets. But the last step often result in the UI layout running away, missing parts, and the texts at weird locations. I have to manually adjust and finetune the layout, but I am still learning about Uiux logic and not so confident in my own "artistic sense", so I wonder if there's a smarter way to do this.

Thanks for reading! Would love to hear some cool advice and notes for exchange.

comments.author: Professional-Mark283
comments.body:
I'm currently working on a rhythm game and its crazy how 1-to-1 you can get AI mockups to be in-game with a bit of effort. I don't use Claude, I use ChatGPT and Astra/Codex, but hopefully you can use the same workflow if you want

First, here's a screenshot of how it currently looks and plays in game

https://preview.redd.it/md1huyv4ptph1.png?width=1280&format=png&auto=webp&s=bae2d2411483ce4455e0ab01a2ac62e5d970940f

  
Basic workflow I use is telling chatgpt, what I want/expect; if you were making a pause menu and you knew that it should have 3 options like 'Resume' 'Options' and 'Exit' you'd tell it that, as well as any other details. Don't be afraid to also make rough mockups by hand, or just use references from other games and send screenshots of those. In my particular case, my game is inspired by an old flash game rhythm game series called 'super guitar hero maniac deluxe' and I sent screenshots of it when asking it to design the UI.

When I had tried this method before the more recent AI updates, I had always gotten very good results, but was never able to actually use any of the assets in the mockup themselves because they always had some sort of artifacts or GPT wasn't able to extract them cleanly. After Astra came out, when Im done making the exact assets I want in GPT, i ask Astra to extract them one at a time and it works 99% of the time, with me very rarely needing to tell it to clean up some of the assets

For the UI coding itself, I usually send the coding agent a mockup of how it should look first and have it try to do it or if the UI is simple i'll just place it by hand myself. Then ill do multiple passes for adding things like game juice, like having an option glow when selected, and etc. Hope any of this helps, ending advice would probably be to not try and one-shot with a mega prompt; multiple smaller prompts usually worked more well for me

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body:
Thanks! That is pretty helpful. I've heard some good things about Astra in this sub. I will consider incorporate it to my workflow along with Claude. 

That's a pretty sweet layout. Im actually thinking of adding some rhythm mini games in future update. What are the tips of creating a rhythm game? I haven't explored into it yet, do you manually create the timing of when player should tap the button to match the music, or AI can handle this part as well?

replies.author: Professional-Mark283
replies.body: Glad I could help! As for tips on the rhythm game, I more or less used the same methodology that I did for the UI. I told GPT that it should be 4 lanes, use the arrow keys, etc. Then it wrote a prompt I could give to astra for a basic prototype that required no assets. It made some variables like 'perfect\_timing' and 'ok\_timing' that can easily be tweaked, so I didn't have to do anything on that part, so yeah the AI can definitely handle it

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body: Ask Claude to generate a in game editor for HUD for you, make it open on some button, any button, let's say it's "P". So you press "P" Editor opens, you press on a HUD element, some sort of button "move element" and move it wherever you feel like, then press "Save" and it saves new position. Ask it to make it look properly on every monitor when you save them on your resolution. Have editor work similar to photoshop where it will give you helpers and snapping on "helper lines" that show if element you are working on is on the same height, width etc with other elements, so you don't miss align it few pixels (for example you eye it out but make it lower than some other element for few pixels). On top of that you need generated assets (use ChatGPT for image generation) because I honestly do not think you can generate good UI elements without using assets and by doing it all in code.

comments.author: sirpalee
comments.body: I use Astra. Usually give it some example games and screenshots and have some strong directives in mu agents.md about not including unnecessary text everywhere. It tends to use the same color scheme and plaster all sorts of redundant information on the screen everywhere it can.
